From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Market pressure snapshot: pricing moves & model release cadence

Team —

Attaching a brief snapshot ahead of QBR prep. High-level takeaways from field and public releases over the last 10 days:

- Pricing compression: two mid-market vendors (public posts) announced token-price reductions of ~20% for text-gen endpoints; one vendor is bundling embeddings as a discounted add-on. Impact: pressure in PLG trials and renewed pricing questions from several seed-mid market accounts.
- Model release cadence: a major open-model maintainer pushed a smaller, quantized variant this week (faster inference at lower cost) — early benchmarks show parity on common NLU tasks for short prompts.
- Positioning gap: competitors are messaging "cost parity with proprietary stacks"; some field teams report this resonates strongly with finance buyers.

Implications for our QBR narrative / OKR check-ins:
1) Sales org will need crisp cost-defense bullets (how batching + caching + routing preserves latency while lowering unit costs).
2) Product/Runtime should confirm whether any recent kernel/quantization improvements change our recommended configs for mid-market customers; we should be ready to publish a short note.
3) CS/Field ask: flag top-10 accounts where the new messaging could trigger renewal concerns — I included Edge Analytics (see attachments).

Attachments: pricing_comparison_Q2.xlsx (field pricing calls), model_release_timeline.pdf (public release notes + quick take). Also added two drive links in the metadata.

Quick asks:
- Laura: can you share any early renewal churn signals from the accounts you track?
- Marissa: can you ask AE reps to surface any concrete pricing objections by EOD Wed so we can synthesize?
- Markus + Stephanie: can you prepare a 2-slide playbook for QBR: one slide on messaging, one on ops/tech mitigations?

Two-paragraph summary for exec slide deck: we need to acknowledge public cost moves, emphasize Redwood's reliability/rollout & cost controls, and highlight quick wins (route to cheaper variants, per-route batching).

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Field Strategy
Redwood Inference

Note: replying-all preferred so we have a single source of truth for QBR notes.
